Title: Safety and efficacy of dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnant women with HIV from Gabon and Mozambique: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: González et al.
Comment: The modified-ITT low-birthweight analysis is available-case: 315/332 randomised intervention participants and 328/334 randomised control participants had birthweight outcome data. The paper reports 50/315 versus 44/328, not event counts over the full randomised denominators. Do not replace these reported totals with 332 and 334. The reported RR slightly differs from the crude ratio calculated directly from the displayed counts, consistent with the paper's country-adjusted modified Poisson analysis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Daily co-trimoxazole plus IPTp with dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomised, multicentre, two-arm, placebo-controlled, superiority, double-blind clinical trial
domain: Malaria prevention in pregnancy among women with HIV
Medium: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine plus daily oral co-trimoxazole
Topic of Content: Prevention of malaria and adverse pregnancy outcomes
Participant type: Pregnant women with HIV receiving daily co-trimoxazole prophylaxis and antiretroviral therapy
Recruitment source: Women attending the first antenatal-care clinic visit at five study sites in Gabon and Mozambique
Outcome measurement: Newborn birthweight; low birthweight defined as birthweight <2500 g
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher low-birth-weight risk with CTXp plus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; reported RR 1.18.

Title: Intermittent Preventive Treatment With Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for the Prevention of Malaria Among HIV-Infected Pregnant Women
Author: Natureeba et al.
Comment: The trial randomized 100 women per arm, but low birth weight was reported for 99 control and 98 intervention participants. The paper used a modified intention-to-treat approach including women with evaluable outcomes, and Table 2 states these birth-outcome data were limited to gestational age ≥28 weeks. Thus the extracted denominators are available-case analyzed totals, not the full randomized denominators requested for a strict ITT analysis.
domain: Malaria prevention and adverse birth outcomes in HIV-infected pregnancy
Study Environment: Tororo District Hospital antenatal clinic, the AIDS Support Organization, and other health centers in Tororo District; all participants received an insecticide-treated net in an area where indoor residual spraying had recently been implemented
Medium: Monthly oral dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine or matching placebo added to daily oral TMP-SMX
Participant type: HIV-1-infected pregnant women at 12–28 weeks of gestation
Recruitment source: Tororo District Hospital antenatal clinic, the AIDS Support Organization, and other health centers in Tororo District
Outcome measurement: Birth weight measured at delivery; low birth weight defined as <2500 g
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher low-birth-weight risk with CTXp plus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; reported RR 1.01.

Title: Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy with Mefloquine in HIV-Infected Women Receiving Cotrimoxazole Prophylaxis: A Multicenter Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
Author: González et al.
Comment: The paper calls this ITT, but its methods define the outcome-specific ITT cohort as randomized women with data available for that outcome. Thus, the reported low-birth-weight denominators (486 control and 489 MQ; N=975) are available-case denominators rather than the full randomized-arm denominators (537 control and 534 MQ). Do not substitute randomized totals for the reported outcome denominators without a separate prespecified sensitivity analysis.
Design Type: Multicenter individually randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial
domain: Malaria prevention in pregnancy among women with HIV
Study Environment: Antenatal care clinics in five sites in sub-Saharan Africa
Medium: Daily cotrimoxazole prophylaxis, intermittent preventive treatment tablets, and long-lasting insecticide-treated net
Content length: Three monthly IPTp doses given at least one month apart
Topic of Content: Mefloquine added to cotrimoxazole prophylaxis for malaria prevention during pregnancy
Recruitment source: Pregnant women attending antenatal care clinics for the first time
Outcome measurement: Newborns were weighed, including stillbirths; weights not captured at birth were estimated from weights obtained in the first week using a regression model.
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher low-birth-weight risk with CTXp plus mefloquine; reported RR 1.32.

Title: Chemoprevention for malaria with monthly intermittent preventive treatment with dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine in pregnant women living with HIV on daily co-trimoxazole in Kenya and Malawi: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Barsosio et al.
Comment: The paper reports available-case modified intention-to-treat denominators for low birthweight (422 intervention and 433 control), rather than the full randomised-arm denominators (448 and 456). Thus 26 randomised intervention participants and 23 randomised control participants were not included in this birthweight result. The extracted primary direct comparison is the paper-labelled unadjusted RR, whose model included stratification factors site and HIV status as covariates.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Daily co-trimoxazole plus monthly dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Multicentre, individually randomised, double-blind, two-arm placebo-controlled trial
domain: Malaria chemoprevention in pregnancy and HIV
Study Environment: Six antenatal clinics in areas with perennial malaria transmission and high-grade sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine resistance
Medium: Monthly oral intermittent preventive treatment added to daily oral co-trimoxazole
Participant type: Pregnant women living with HIV on dolutegravir-based combination antiretroviral therapy with viable singleton pregnancies at 16–28 weeks' gestation
Recruitment source: Six antenatal clinics in western Kenya and Malawi
effect_direction: RR > 1 indicates higher low-birth-weight risk with CTXp plus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; reported unadjusted RR 1.10.

Title: Cotrimoxazole Prophylaxis Versus Mefloquine Intermittent Preventive Treatment to Prevent Malaria in HIV-Infected Pregnant Women: Two Randomized Controlled Trials
Author: Denoeud-Ndam et al.
Comment: Table 2 reports low-birth-weight outcomes only among live singleton births with available birth weight: 126 in the CTX-alone arm and 119 in the CTX + MQ-IPTp arm. The trial randomized 146 women per arm, but the Results do not report low-birth-weight event counts using those randomized denominators. Therefore, event totals are recorded exactly as the reported mITT available-case counts and must not be treated as randomized-arm denominators. No risk ratio or confidence interval was reported by the paper.
Design Type: Parallel open-label randomized noninferiority controlled trial
domain: Malaria prevention and pregnancy outcomes in HIV-infected women
Study Environment: Five urban hospitals implementing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV programs
Medium: Daily oral cotrimoxazole prophylaxis with or without supervised mefloquine intermittent preventive treatment
Participant type: HIV-infected pregnant women with CD4 counts below 350/mm3 or advanced HIV disease
Recruitment source: Five urban hospitals in Cotonou and Porto-Novo implementing a prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV program
Outcome measurement: Live singleton infant with birth weight below 2500 g
effect_direction: RR < 1 indicates lower low-birth-weight risk with CTXp plus mefloquine; crude RR is calculable from 24/119 intervention vs 26/126 control.
